column1: # ID || Short title || Manuscript location || Kind || Assessment (root-authored)

STRATA D.1 || Exceptional adjunctions for open and closed pieces || 105/043–047, two-open construction || unpursued implication || The two-open diagram is present, but no exceptional adjunction chain for a complementary open/closed pair is constructed. The phrase “carré abstrait σ” on 047 concerns coherent excision, so this is a partial thematic antecedent rather than a form of the six-operation assertion.

STRATA D.2 || Pointed fibres, cofibres, and stable exactness || 105/050, final Der 6; 052, upper left || conjecture / withdrawn in the same text || “σ est cartésien ssi il est cocartésien” proposes the relevant exactness principle, but without the pointed stable hypotheses of the context row. The assertion about Hot is then marked “Complètement faux” on 052, so the package records a proposed principle and its unstable obstruction, not the full stable theorem or a triangulation construction.

STRATA D.3 || Proper and smooth lifting criteria for posets || 105/045 and 051 || unpursued implication || The use of “propre” for the cofibred replacement and of “lisse” for ρ gives a fibrewise base-change method. No poset lifting-category criterion or necessity-and-sufficiency proof appears, so the context classification is not restated here.

STRATA D.4 || Proper/smooth base change || 105/045, fibre calculation; 051, counit calculation || unpursued implication || The manuscript uses properness and smoothness in concrete Kan-extension calculations, a close instance of the context's base-change mechanism. Its “φ̄ est propre” argument does not formulate the complete arbitrary-square theorem or its converse, and the excision conclusion on 046 retains a verification flag.

STRATA D.5 || Failure of a naive geometric properness criterion || 105/002–053, no corresponding example || source comparison; no form found || No proposed topological characterization of proper poset maps, and no counterexample to one, occurs. The categorical “propre” of 045 is used for base change and cannot be equated with a geometric criterion merely by name.

STRATA D.6 || A diamond map beyond strict (op)fibrations || 105/046–053, square-shaped indexing diagrams || source comparison; no form found || The diamond drawings encode coherent squares and excision, not the specific finite-poset map distinguishing smooth/proper maps from strict fibrations and opfibrations. No such separating example or bundle claim is supplied.

STRATA D.7 || Inclusions and product projections || 105/043–045 and 051 || unpursued implication || The two-open sieve construction and a particular proper/smooth ρ are present, but there is no general classification of poset inclusions or product projections. These are examples used inside an argument, not a statement of all the context row's criteria.

STRATA D.8 || Finite-poset geometric dictionary || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No realization-stratification dictionary or comparison of constructible base-change operations is developed. The four-vertex square shapes near the end do not supply that geometric interpretation.

STRATA D.9 || Specialization and slice variance correction || 105/043, open-sieve convention || reading question / source comparison || The source fixes a two-open categorical cover, but does not give the context's formula involving y\\X and closure of a point. Accordingly it neither states nor corrects the particular variance error in the later companion; the directions of its own diagrams remain frozen independently.

STRATA G.2 || Totality and universal homotopy-colimit correctness || 105/018 and 034–040, filtering limits || source comparison; no form found || No equivalence between total asphericity and all simplicial homotopy-colimit comparisons is stated. “filtering direct limits” here belongs to closure and accessibility for factorization and is not the context's universal comparison property.

PATHS A.P1 || Components of full path categories || 105/003, cancelled Ch(C) sheet || unpursued implication || The notation “Ch(C)” appears, but the sheet discusses its projections rather than identifying π₀ of path categories with localized Hom sets. No full-path definition or component calculation is supplied, so the context proposition has no stated form here.

PATHS A.P2 || Sequential and all-type path comparisons || 105/003, cancelled Ch(C) sheet || source comparison; no form found || There is no sequence of path types or fibred-roof comparison. The W∞-fibration question does not establish equivalence between sequential and all-type constructions.

PATHS A.1 || Grothendieck construction for span roofs || 105/045 and 048–049, total categories || unpursued implication || “la cat. cofibrée ... qu'il définit” on 048 gives a Grothendieck-construction method for a span used in excision. It does not identify the path-category roof construction or prove the comparison in the context row; the common method is the connection.

PATHS A.2 || Filtered Cat-colimits and total categories || 105/038–040, filtering-limit closure || source comparison; no form found || The filtering-colimit discussion concerns lifting classes in M, not the map from a Grothendieck total category to an ordinary colimit of categories. No weak-equivalence theorem for that comparison is stated or proved.

PATHS A.3 || Universal total-functor criterion || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The package does not formulate the context's condition on every functor and every u/t. The comma fibres used on 045 serve a specific right-Kan calculation and do not provide the universal criterion.

PATHS A.4 || Insufficiency of preorder cofinality and parallel homotopy || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No such sufficient-condition proposal or counterexample appears. The ordinal choices in the small-object argument do not concern cofinality in a path-type preorder.

PATHS A.5 || Total shapes can give incorrect Cat-colimits || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || Neither Δ_inj nor the diagram of monoid categories BN^(n+1) occurs. The source's use of filtered limits supplies no example separating total asphericity from ordinary Cat-colimit correctness.

PATHS A.6 || Δ_inj is total and exact but not filtered || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No Δ_inj counterexample, exactness calculation, or total-asphericity assertion appears. This is the same absence recorded for NEW_RESULTS 11, not a reason to reinterpret “filtering” in the English argument.

PATHS A.7 || Three classes of indexing shapes || 105/018 and 034–040, nearest different use || source comparison; no form found || The hierarchy from filtered categories through universally correct Cat-colimit shapes to total shapes is not stated. The manuscript assumes filtering where needed for factorization and does not compare those three classes.

PATHS A.8 || Classification of Cat-colimit shapes remains open || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No intrinsic classification of universally correct Cat-colimit shapes is attempted. The unfinished removal of smallness on 040 is a different open problem and cannot settle this row.

PATHS A.9 || Subdivision map without a Cat_hot inverse || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no triangle-boundary face poset, subdivision map, or enumeration of reverse monotone maps. The natural homotopies on 052 concern a total-category inclusion and are not the context counterexample.

PATHS B.1 || Full and weak-vertical path diagrams || 105/003, Ch(C); 052, short homotopies || unpursued implication || The path notation on the cancelled sheet does not define which vertical arrows are allowed or prove strict compatibility with concatenation. The length-2 homotopy described on 052 is a particular natural-transformation zigzag, not a construction of both path diagrams.

PATHS B.2 || Weak-vertical paths and hammocks || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No hammock mapping simplicial set or reduction to it is constructed. Lifting-class and factorization arguments do not by themselves furnish a mapping-space comparison.

PATHS B.3 || Literal inclusion J need not be an isomorphism || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The manuscript does not introduce J or a marking on the vertical maps of paths. Its saturation questions therefore do not give the specific counterexample claimed by this row.

PATHS B.4 || Isomorphism markings and all-arrow markings || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || Neither extremal marking case is analyzed for full path categories. The all-coefficient remark on 046 concerns ξ and is unrelated to marking all arrows of a path construction.

PATHS B.5 || Homotopy fractions on the restricted side || 105/025–030, localization and saturation || unpursued implication || “W is strongly saturated” is discussed, but no homotopy calculus of fractions or short-fraction comparison is stated. The uncertain isolated word “Relations|fractions” on 030 cannot carry such a theorem.

PATHS B.6 || Coherent full-path map to localization mapping spaces || 105/003 and 046–047, different coherence issues || source comparison; no form found || No coherent map from a full path space to a localization mapping space, or split-monic conclusion for J, appears. The coherent-square distinction on 047 is conceptually related but supplies none of the required construction.

PATHS B.7 || Padding backward squares into hammocks || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || Identity padding and mixed-boundary hammock sweeps are absent. The lifting squares attached in 034 are cells in a factorization construction, not squares of path morphisms.

PATHS B.8 || Whether J is always a weak equivalence || 105/003, cancelled path question || source comparison; no form found || “C'est une chose à vérifier” concerns the endpoint projection's fibration property, not J. The package does not resolve or restate the unrestricted-vertical comparison problem.

PATHS B.9 || Finite search of 132 comparisons || 105/006–041, recycled computing sheets || source comparison; no form found || No path-category search, F₂ homology table, or count of 132 comparisons is present. The reused job and program output is unrelated evidence and is not repurposed as a verification of this claim.

PATHS C.P1 || Categories of endpoint-preserving type maps || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The source does not define the increasing maps between path types or their enriched composition. Its interval I in the topos construction is a different object with a different role.

PATHS C.P2 || Descent to a reachability preorder || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no reachability preorder of path types or descent of a coherent path-space diagram. The transfinite ordinal indexing on 034–040 is not the sequential cofinality result in this row.

PATHS C.P3 || The three CATHOT E.26 comparisons || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No wide-marking theorem or three-comparison statement is present. The use of Hot_W on 052 only locates an excision square and supplies no form of those path-space comparisons.

PATHS C.P4 || Mixed-sign blocks and composition in Hot || 105/052, length-2 homotopy, nearest limited connection || source comparison; no form found || The manuscript describes two composites homotopic to an inclusion, but gives no block padding, mixed-sign condition, or associative unital composition theorem. This local homotopy does not state the context's block independence.

PATHS C.P5 || q_L can fail to be invertible in Cat_hot || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no q_L comparison or four-object crown example. The four-vertex square category used for derivator axioms is not that counterexample.

PATHS C.1 || Strict enrichment by all-type paths || 105/003, cancelled Ch(C) question || unpursued implication || The Ch(C) notation points toward a path construction, but strict units, associativity, enrichment, nerves, and Kan replacement are not developed. The sheet's tentative W∞-fibration claim cannot be promoted to the enrichment theorem.

PATHS C.2 || Hammock composition and simplicial localization || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No composition-compatible hammock model is stated. The factorization methods concern arrows of M and do not compare mapping simplicial sets.

PATHS C.3 || Failure of pointed Cartesian units || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || A pointed Cartesian path-composition law and the zero-object unit obstruction are absent. The candidate bicartesian axiom does not address this unit calculation.

PATHS C.4 || Kan mapping spaces for pointed simplicial objects || 105/027, cancelled Hom(I,Y) passage || unpursued implication || The manuscript writes that an internal-Hom endpoint map is a Kan fibration and asks about Serre fibrations. It does not supply the context's cofibrant–fibrant pointed simplicial mapping-space statement, and the cancelled passage leaves the ambient assumptions undeveloped.

PATHS C.5 || Quillen groupoid from derived mapping spaces || 105/025–030, Quillen terminology || source comparison; no form found || “Quillen pair” and “Quillen triple” describe lifting and factorization, not the fundamental groupoid of a derived mapping space. No identification of that groupoid appears.

PATHS C.6 || Loop and suspension formulas || 105/050, proposed cartesian/cocartesian axiom || unpursued implication || The phrase “cartésien ssi ... cocartésien” suggests a setting in which loop/suspension comparisons would matter. No pointed loop or suspension formula is stated, so the context row is a possible consequence to investigate under additional hypotheses, not a manuscript theorem.

PATHS C.7 || Representability of π₁ versus loop formulas || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The source makes no representability claim for π₁ of a mapping space and does not distinguish it from a loop-object formula. The path-fibration question on 003 supplies neither assertion.

PATHS C.8 || Derived Hom complexes || 105/007–012, internal Hom in a topos || source comparison; no form found || The underlined Hom is used in a tensor/Hom lifting adjunction, not a derived Hom complex of additive or chain-complex coefficients. Thus the shared notation does not provide the context result.

PATHS C.9 || General additive path proposal || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No additive path-category theory is proposed. The dualizing-functor speculation on 050 does not assume additivity or solve the open additive comparison.

PATHS C.10 || Pointed ind-path problem || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || Pointed ind-path objects and their comparison problem are absent. The smallness assumptions of 034–040 concern generating arrows, not ind-objects representing mapping invariants.

PATHS D.1 || The three Chapter IX diagram tests || 105/046–052, coherent square discussion || unpursued implication || The distinction between an abstract square and its “diagramme squelettique” is relevant to diagram testing. The three Chapter IX conditions themselves are not formulated or compared here.

PATHS D.2 || Five-arrow pointed counterexample || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No five-arrow pointed category or counterexample to a diagram test is given. The finite square and fork shapes are indexing categories, not the claimed relative-category example.

PATHS D.3 || Finite products force a finite category to be a preorder || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No finite-category product classification is stated. Product closure in the topos lifting argument concerns classes of maps and is mathematically different.

PATHS D.4 || Rectification implies constant-shape tests || 105/046–047, coherent versus skeletal diagrams || unpursued implication || The manuscript insists on the coherent σ behind its skeletal square. It gives no general rectification hypothesis or derivation of the constant-shape tests, so only the need for coherent data is shared.

PATHS D.5 || Six-object suspension restriction counterexample || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No six-object suspension or failure of restriction is constructed. The shape Q on 046 is used for Kan extension, not this counterexample.

PATHS D.6 || Loop formulas imply representability || 105/050–052, nearest possible structural link || source comparison; no form found || The source does not state a loop formula or infer representability from one. Its provisional square axioms cannot replace the missing pointed representability argument.

PATHS D.7 || Rectification for derivable categories || 105/034–040, factorization method || unpursued implication || Functorial factorization is explicitly asserted, but the package does not construct diagram categories of a derivable category or prove their rectification comparison. This is a method potentially usable in such a proof, not the theorem in the row.

PATHS D.8 || Intrinsic cofibrations and finite rectification || 105/030–032, recognition and properness conditions || unpursued implication || The Quillen-triple criterion and additional “strict” base/cobase-change condition are close structural input. No finite-shape rectification conclusion or full intrinsic-cofibration axiom package is written, so the relationship is partial.

PATHS D.9 || Finite counterexamples to cofibration axioms || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The diamond and finite-set counterexamples to CF5/CF6 are absent. Nothing about the square-shaped derivator diagrams supplies those relative-category examples.

PATHS D.10 || Cubes do not test all finite posets || 105/051–052, shifted square axioms || unpursued implication || The request to impose an axiom on all D_I acknowledges diagramwise structure, but the manuscript does not claim that cubes test every finite poset. It therefore supplies neither the false implication nor the context counterexample.

PATHS D.11 || Finite semisimplicial tests versus BZ and BK || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No distinction between finite-poset tests and BZ/BK diagram shapes occurs. The finitely presented special case on 036 is about accessibility, not rectification at those shapes.

PATHS D.12 || A contractible fence can fail BK rectification || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no fence example or comparison with BK. The early path notation alone does not identify an eventual-fence construction.

PATHS D.13 || Localization by a relative poset does not imply rectification || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No replacement by a relative poset is constructed. The cofibred replacement on 045 is used for a specific cohomology square and is not a rectification theorem for all diagrams.

PATHS D.14 || Shape audit of Kaledin's framework || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No Kaledin-type enhancement or audit of its allowed indexing shapes is present. The package's small and finite diagram shapes cannot be used to supply hypotheses absent from the later comparison.

PATHS D.15 || Naive Pos-enhancement criterion || 105/046–047 and 051, diagramwise distinctions || unpursued implication || The source separates coherent objects of D(Q) from their skeletal diagrams and asks for shifted versions. It neither defines the naive Pos-enhancement nor proves its equivalence criterion, so this is a conceptual antecedent only.

PATHS D.16 || Circle and infinite-additivity failure || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No infinite-additivity counterexample indexed by a circle is given. The colimit hypotheses in the factorization section are assumptions, not a calculation of this failure.

PATHS D.17 || Finite versus all-shape cofibration axioms || 105/018, 034–040 || unpursued implication || “filtering direct limits” and the continuous transfinite lemma make closure under larger constructions explicit. The source does not state the finite/all-shape rectification dichotomy, but records the sort of additional closure input that such a distinction needs.

PATHS D.18 || Accessible localizers and Thomason model structures || 105/020, 030–032, and 040 || stated goal / unpursued implication || “What remains to be understood” on 032 asks how the generator description recovers `C∩W`, and 040 retains small generators. This is a close model-recognition program, not a proof of the full accessible-localizer Thomason theorem or a removal of its accessibility hypothesis.

PATHS D.19 || Locally constant full faithfulness need not satisfy two-of-three || 105/047, cancelled locally constant clause || source comparison; no form found || The cancelled clause concerns coefficient scope and a proposed complete equivalence. It does not define the class in this row or prove a failure of two-of-three, so cancellation cannot be cited as its counterexample.

PATHS D.20 || Ho Fun and Fun Ho differ || 105/046–047, abstract versus skeletal square || unpursued implication || “plus précisément ... le carré abstrait σ” explicitly locates the property in D(Q), not merely in the visible commuting square. This is a direct precursor of the distinction in the row, although no general nonfaithfulness example or full comparison theorem is supplied.

PATHS D.21 || All shape tests force an infinity-equivalence || 105/051, margin on D_I || unpursued implication || The manuscript asks for the axiom on shifted derivators, so arbitrary diagram parameters are relevant. It does not formulate the context's A×J testing condition or derive an infinity-categorical equivalence, and those stronger quantifiers must not be inferred.

PATHS D.22 || Open recognition and nonaccessible localizers || 105/032 and 040, final lines || self-flagged / method || “Next step is to try to get rid of this” explicitly leaves the small-generator restriction in place. The construction contributes a conditional method to the open recognition problem but gives no nonaccessible recognition theorem or general accessibility result.

PATHS D.23 || Homology localizers and intrinsic fibrations || 105/022 and 032 || unpursued implication || Base-change stability along F is an added goal, not claimed for every cohomologically defined W. The later negative claims about intrinsic fibrations therefore limit a possible generalization of the program rather than contradicting a completed theorem on these pages.

PATHS D.K1 || Acyclic maps are epimorphic in Hot || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No epimorphism assertion for acyclic maps in Hot is stated. The excision square is a different use of the homotopy category.

PATHS D.K2 || Large acyclic simple groups || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No group construction or small-quotient obstruction appears. The cardinal parameters in the small-object argument have no such group-theoretic interpretation.

PATHS D.K3 || The cardinal Kan–Thurston statement || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The package contains no BG→W construction or bound on homomorphisms into small groups. This absence agrees with the comparison under NEW_RESULTS 3.

PATHS D.K4 || Invariant ind-objects reflect to groupoids || 105/003, nearest path notation || source comparison; no form found || No ind-groupoid reflection or W∞-invariance criterion is stated. The tentative fibration property of Ch(C) does not imply that reflection theorem.

PATHS D.K5 || All-shape tests force a one-type || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no conclusion that an object must be a one-type from its shape tests. The small squares and interval tests in the manuscript are not the quantified test family of this row.

PATHS E.1 || Endpoint fibres of all-arrow paths || 105/003, cancelled endpoint projection || conjecture / partial connection || The source's “p:Ch(C)→C×C” is the closest local form, but its path construction and strict fibre identification are not developed. Its explicit verification flag prevents using the sheet as a proof of the later endpoint-fibre theorem.

PATHS E.2 || Strict monoidal loop model || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No strict monoidal loop category or unit/composition calculation is present. The internal Hom of an interval on 027 does not provide that structure.

PATHS E.3 || All-type endpoints smooth but not proper || 105/003, middle of cancelled sheet || reading question / partial connection || The source says p is not cohomologically proper or smooth, whereas the context row distinguishes properties of a specified all-type construction. This is a potential difference to investigate, not a certified contradiction, because the exact Ch(C) and coefficient conventions on the sheet have not been identified with that later construction.

PATHS E.4 || Eventual endpoints smooth and proper, not strict || 105/003, cancelled path projection || source comparison; no form found || The text separates categorical and cohomological fibration language but gives no eventual-fence definition or theorem with both properties. Its tentative statements cannot be transferred to the eventual model simply because both are called paths.

PATHS E.5 || Functorial mapping-path replacement || 105/003 and 034–038 || unpursued implication || There is an endpoint-fibration question and a separate functorial cellular factorization method. No mapping-path replacement is constructed from them, so the manuscript supplies two related ingredients in different settings rather than the context factorization.

PATHS E.6 || Rectangular-band monoid counterexample || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No rectangular-band monoid or strictification counterexample is given. The cancelled path discussion has no such finite witness.

PATHS E.7 || Interval pushout-products versus intrinsic Cat-cofibrations || 105/012–018, topos construction || reading question / limited comparison || The interval pushout-product is present in a topos with monomorphisms as C. The row's failure for intrinsic cofibrations in Cat has different ambient hypotheses, so it does not refute the same assertion as written here.

PATHS E.8 || Finite interval cotensors can have wrong fibres || 105/027, cancelled Hom(I,Y) discussion || unpursued implication || The Kan/Serre question makes interval endpoint maps relevant, but there is no proof of the needed fibre formula or the counterexample in this row. This is a warning against filling in that formula from the notation alone.

PATHS E.9 || W∞-smooth/proper does not imply larger-W fibration || 105/002–003 and 032 || unpursued implication || The early lemmas explicitly use W∞, and the English section separately asks for properness relative to its selected W and F. The manuscript does not assert the invalid passage to every larger localizer, so the context row supplies a boundary on generalization.

PATHS E.10 || Marking components is not a stratification || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No component marking or stratification theorem appears. The two-open categorical cover is not a definition of a marked-component stratification.

PATHS E.11 || Open strict bifibration replacement R || 105/003, final cancelled question || conjecture / partial connection || The question about W∞-fibrations and a Quillen structure signals interest in replacement maps but does not construct R or prove strict bifibration. It therefore adds historical evidence of the issue without settling the open row.

PATHS E.12 || Fixed-origin paths: contractible versus total/filtered || 105/003, Ch(C) sheet || source comparison; no form found || Fixed-origin path categories, total asphericity, and filteredness are not related on this sheet. In particular the fibration speculation is not a statement that path categories are total or filtered.

PATHS E.13 || Finite Yoneda data need not be faithful || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || There is no finite-Yoneda embedding or nonfaithfulness example. The skeletal/coherent distinction is relevant background but does not state this particular obstruction.

BISITE A.1 || Saturation conventions and Theorem A variants || 105/005, 025, 027–028 || reading question / partial antecedent || The source explicitly distinguishes “mild saturation,” direct factors, and “strongly saturated,” while questioning relations among them. This supplies historical forms for the terminology discussion, but does not formulate the context's absolute/relative Theorem A distinction.

BISITE A.2 || Intrinsic fibrations as universal pullback preservation || 105/022, item d; 032, condition 4 || unpursued implication || “W stable by base changes by any g∈F” is demanded as an extra property of a Quillen triple. F itself is defined by RLP here, so this is not a definition or proof identifying the entire intrinsic-fibration class with the universal pullback-preserving class.

BISITE A.3 || Slice, universal, and local weak-equivalence classes || 105/016–018, UW interval condition || unpursued implication || The boxed universal condition `(I−e)∈UW` is a genuine local form of a universal-W notion. The full family of slice and fine/local equivalence classes in the context row is not defined or compared.

BISITE A.4 || Postcomposition and raw pullback || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No general statement about postcomposition between localized slices and raw pullback is made. The pullback stability desired on 032 is restricted to the selected F, not an unrestricted raw-pullback theorem.

BISITE A.5 || Maximal universal test class || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The source does not construct the maximal class defined by all universal tests. Its chosen interval family and orthogonal classes solve a different generation problem.

BISITE A.6 || Transporter Galois connection || 105/025, lifting polarity || unpursued implication || “order reversing bijections” describes the left/right lifting polarity on saturated classes. This is formally analogous to the context's transporter Galois connection but has a different defining relation, so the two constructions are not identified.

BISITE A.7 || Transporter composition criterion || 105/025 and 040, closure under composition || source comparison; no form found || The closure results concern orthogonal lifting classes and continuous cellular composites. They do not state or prove the context's transporter-composition criterion.

BISITE A.8 || Failure of transporter composition || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No chain example showing failure of transporter composition is supplied. The manuscript's composition assumptions are not a claim that arbitrary transporters compose.

BISITE A.9 || Smooth/proper stabilizers versus intrinsic fibrations || 105/002–003 and 045 || unpursued implication || The early French sheets distinguish W∞-properness, smoothness, and fibration language, and 045 uses categorical cofibredness to obtain properness. They do not define both stabilizer classes or give the full comparison with intrinsic fibrations, so the evidence is terminological and methodological.

BISITE A.10 || Three fibre axioms and slice localization || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No three-axiom package for intermediate fibre categories or equivalence of their localizations appears. The two lifting factorizations are different data.

BISITE A.11 || Factorization implies Fib∩W equals universal W || 105/030–032 || unpursued implication || The retract proof obtains `F∩W=TF` for the selected Quillen classes, and the next page separately adds properness. It does not state the general intrinsic identity `Fib_W∩W=W_u`, although the conditional model framework is a natural place to compare it.

BISITE A.12 || Functorial replacement and intermediate localizations || 105/036–038, functorial factorization || unpursued implication || A functorial factorization is explicitly claimed after the small-object construction. The source does not use it to prove equivalence of every intermediate slice localization, so the relation is a possible method rather than a form of that theorem.

BISITE A.13 || Six-object failure of the third fibre axiom || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || No six-object example separating fibre axioms a, b, and c is present. The author's distinct a–d list on 022 concerns model recognition and must not be confused with those axioms.

BISITE A.14 || Fine axioms || 105/002–053, no form found || source comparison; no form found || The package does not state the fine-slice axiom system. Its topos and test-category discussion is a related ambient setting, not the fine formalism itself.

BISITE A.15 || Four fibration classes and Loc(7) || 105/002–003 and 032 || unpursued implication || W∞-proper, W∞-smooth, W∞-perfect, and fibration language occurs, with several conclusions unproved or uncertain. There is no complete four-class comparison or Loc(7) equivalence theorem, and the separate property 4 on 032 remains an additional requirement.

BISITE A.16 || ABC transfer through replacements || 105/034–038, cellular factorization || unpursued implication || The explicit functorial factorization is a possible replacement method. The manuscript does not formulate an ABC transfer theorem or verify the required hypotheses for transferred diagram or slice structures.

BISITE A.17 || Brown/ABC criterion with terminal hypotheses || 105/030–032 || source comparison; no form found || The Quillen-triple criterion and its properness addition are present, but no Brown/ABC equivalence with the specified terminal-object assumptions is stated. Those terminal hypotheses cannot be inferred from the existence of the terminal symbol e in individual diagrams.

BISITE A.18 || Weak constant-coefficient maps may fail composition || 105/045–047, coefficient discussion || unpursued implication || The manuscript moves between constant and locally constant coefficients and cancels one attempted qualification.
